title: Core30 intake research output
description: The machine-readable contract between entity research (docs/intake/entity-research-prompt.md) and the build. Its purpose is that research drops STRAIGHT into site.config + the content tree with no human retyping — the drift the whole starter exists to kill (one NAP fact was copied into five documents on the donor sites). `entities[]` is the content-tree seed; `business`/`compliance` map onto site.config.json. Nothing here is fabricated: every fact carries provenance, and anything unverified is marked, never guessed.

vertical.description: The industry preset id this research targets (e.g. 'auto', 'concrete', 'hvac'). Selects the preset that validates schemaType and supplies the entity vocabulary. For a GREENFIELD project with no chosen vertical yet, this may be a new preset id the project defines.

posture.description: GREENFIELD = no Google Business Profile exists yet: the research OUTPUT DEFINES the GBP categories/services to create, and page-build approval comes from the owner, not from a GBP description. EXISTING-GBP = a live GBP exists: pages are gated by whether the GBP entry has a customer-facing description (the ghost rule). See gbp-alignment.md. The gbpDescribed field on each entity is only meaningful when posture is existing-gbp.

business.description: Maps onto site.config.json -> business, verbatim. `_provenance` records where each fact came from so an unverified value is never silently promoted to the page.

primaryCategory.description: The GBP primary category, in Google's own wording. Drives the homepage H1 keyphrase.

geo.description: Real coordinate or null. NEVER fabricate — a wrong coordinate maps the business to an address it does not occupy.

rating.description: Real Google Business Profile numbers only. Omit / leave blank until confirmed — an invented aggregateRating is a rich-result penalty and a Core30 violation.

sameAs.description: The business's OWN authoritative profiles (GBP CID URL, Yelp, Facebook, BBB) — the entity-reconciliation signal. Real URLs only.

_provenance.description: Per-field source: a URL, 'client-stated', or 'UNVERIFIED'. A field marked UNVERIFIED must not render a claim until confirmed.

geoScope.description: Maps onto site.config.json -> geoScope. `buildPage` marks a city that earns its own city×service page vs. one merely named in areaServed.

entities.description: THE core output — the content-tree seed. One entry per distinct entity that passed the ENTITY TEST (see entity-research-prompt.md §Validation). `slug`+`trinity`+`parent`+`schemaType`+`placement` are exactly what a content-tree row needs; `parent` builds the mirror-link graph that core30-lint enforces (charter §8, rule 3).

slug.description: URL keyphrase, kebab-case. Interpolable with {{city}} for city×service multiplication.

trinity.description: The one string that must be <title>, <h1>, and the URL keyphrase (Core30 rule 1). {{city}}/{{state}} tokens allowed; resolved at build.

buyerPhrasing.description: The words real people use for this entity — feeds the goal-completion first sentence (Core30 rule 2). NOT keyword variants; the distinct phrasings buyers actually search.

evidence.description: Where real demand for this entity was observed. One entry is enough; zero means it did not pass the ENTITY TEST and should not be here.

cluster.description: The vertical's grouping axis (e.g. credit-situation, vehicle-segment, service-category). Preset-defined.

schemaType.description: The JSON-LD @type this page emits. Validated by the preset (e.g. auto: AutoDealer|Car|FinancialService|Service).

placement.description: Where this entity lives. One entity, one placement (the donor's locked rule — no entity duplicated across surfaces).

parent.description: slug of the parent entity — builds the mirror-link graph. A page must link up to its parent and the parent must link down to it (Core30 rule 3).

tier.description: Build priority. A = build now, B = core authority, C = niche/post-launch.

gbpDescribed.description: EXISTING-GBP posture only: does the GBP entry for this entity have a customer-facing description? A NO-description entry is a GHOST (Google-suggested, not owner-approved) and gets NO page. IGNORED when posture is greenfield — with no GBP, `ownerApproved` is the build gate instead.

ownerApproved.description: GREENFIELD posture: has the owner approved building this entity into a page (and, later, into a GBP category/service)? With no GBP to gate against, this is the build gate. The never-build-unapproved discipline is preserved; only the source of approval changes.

entityLinks.description: Curated Knowledge-Graph links for the page's about/mentions JSON-LD (schema.js entityLinks). NEVER hand-written — every QID fetched live and label-matched (see gbp-alignment.md §Entity map). A wrong sameAs tells Google the page is about the wrong thing.

gatedBy.description: compliance.claimGates ids that gate content on this page. An item whose gate is unconfirmed does not render (charter §5).

compliance.description: Maps onto site.config.json -> compliance. The per-client legal posture; core30-lint reads it. Every flag defaults to the CONSERVATIVE (claim-suppressing) value — a missing true claim costs some conversion, a present false claim is legal exposure, and those are not symmetric.

allowedClaims.description: Phrases the client MAY use, each with the condition that makes it true (e.g. 'licensed' allowed only where the client holds the license). Polarity is per-client: one vertical bans a word another requires.

claimGates.description: Verified-or-suppressed flags. Each becomes a site.config claimGate defaulting false; the Engine withholds the claim until the owner confirms. `question` is the exact wording the owner answers — the client fact-check questionnaire generates from this list.

publishGate.description: Things that must be true before specific pages go live (e.g. a registration a page depends on). Blocks the named slugs until met.

excludedEntities.description: Entities that are a legal problem to build even though demand exists — captured so the exclusion is a recorded decision, not a silent omission.

localSpecificity.description: Core30 rule 4 ammunition — verifiable local facts (permit names, code limits, corridor names) injectable into copy via {{...}}. Each traces to a source; an unsourced 'local fact' is not one.

externalAuthorities.description: Core30 rule 6 registry — authoritative outbound links (.gov, standards bodies, manufacturer specs). `verified:false` is the machine form of the EXTERNAL-LINK-TODO pattern; core30-lint fails the build on an unverified link at publish.

caveats.description: Facts the researcher is UNCERTAIN about, kept explicit so downstream work does not treat inference as verified. This discipline is why the donor sites do not publish fabricated claims; it must survive the format change.

sameAs.description: Wikipedia URL + Wikidata URL for this entity. Both forms so Google resolves from either graph. Fetched live and label-matched on a dated pass — never hand-written from memory.

verifiedOn.description: ISO date the QID was last live-verified against wikidata.org.
